newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-KANU MAKES GOOD PROGRESS AFTER HEART OP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KANU MAKES GOOD PROGRESS AFTER HEART OP.

text.p: Nigerian international Nwankwo Kanu is making good progress from heart surgery but his Italian club Internazionale said it was still too early to tell whether he would ever play again.
"At the moment it's very difficult to say if he will play soccer again," the serie A club's spokeswoman Susanna Wermelinger said on Thursday. "Kanu's chances of playing soccer again are still low.
"Doctors in the United States have told us that they cannot say if Kanu will play again. It's too early," she added.
The daily Corriere dello Sport newspaper reported on Thursday that American doctors were increasingly optimistic that Kanu would be able to play again.
It quoted unnamed Inter officials as saying that Kanu's return next season could not be ruled out.
Kanu, 20, who captained Nigeria's under-23 team to the Olympic title last summer, had an operation last November at the Cleveland Clinic in the United States.
Doctors had said before the operation that Kanu might never play again. The player has vowed to do everything possible to return.
"We are very satisfied by Kanu's improvement, but it is one thing to be able to walk and another to run and to play soccer" Wermelinger added.
Kanu moved from Ajax to Inter after the Games for a reported fee of around $2 million.
